display.title: Episode 290: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 2 (Rosh Chodesh Elul)
display.summary_short: A Rosh Chodesh Elul show: Hashem as the King in the field, a class sings about the Rambam's Mishneh Torah, the Alter Rebbe's puzzling advice saves Reb Boruch, and why we blow shofar all Elul.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Elul 5747. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul closes the year and prepares for the next, so we daven more carefully, learn more and give more tzedakah, and he shares the Alter Rebbe's parable from Likkutei Torah of the King in the field, who greets everyone warmly and grants their wishes. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Brooklyn yeshiva says the Shema and, led by their rebbe, sings a song naming the fourteen books of the Rambam's Mishneh Torah. Story time concludes 'Saved by a Miracle' (called on air 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik'): Reb Boruch, framed by the jealous Alex for stealing logs, had been told by the Alter Rebbe to skip his summons to the minister. When he finally goes, he learns that an officer had been waiting that very Tuesday to shoot him, and that witnesses have since proved his innocence. The show ends with the Elul shofar: why it is blown without a brachah, and the Rambam's call, 'Wake up, sleepers!'
display.lesson: In Elul Hashem is close like a king in the field; and a tzaddik sees what we cannot, so we trust his guidance even when it seems strange.
